title: Marathon Reveals Major Nightfall Update and December PvE Expansion
summary: Bungie has revealed a major roadmap for Marathon, including refreshed progression, new rewards and a permanent PvE experience planned for December.
content:
Bungie has announced a major update roadmap for Marathon, its sci-fi extraction shooter. The October Nightfall Refresh focuses on progression, rewards and changes designed to improve the overall live experience, while a much larger December update promises to add an entirely new way to play. Together, the two updates give players a clear picture of where the game is heading over the coming months.

The update resets player progression and equipment, refreshes the in-game economy and introduces a new NuCal-inspired Reward Pass at no additional cost to players who own the game. Bungie has also outlined adjustments to weapons, Runner abilities and matchmaking activities. Resetting progression gives everyone a fresh start, and the refreshed economy is intended to make rewards and resources feel more meaningful from the very first match.

The next major milestone is Marathon: Symbiosis, planned for December 8, 2026. It is expected to introduce the game's first permanent PvE experience, an expanded Perimeter, a new Runner shell named Bishop, a social space and a firing range. Bungie has also outlined further connected PvE and PvP experiences for March, showing that the studio intends to keep expanding the game well beyond this year.

## What the October Nightfall Refresh Changes

The Nightfall Refresh is the first step in Bungie's roadmap and is built around progression, rewards and the general health of the live game. Rather than adding a single headline feature, the update touches several systems at once so that the game feels more balanced and rewarding for both new and returning players.

The progression and equipment reset is the most noticeable change. Because everyone begins again, players have the chance to rebuild their loadouts, try different approaches and experience the early stages of the game with a renewed sense of progress. For returning players, this also means that older advantages are removed, and the playing field becomes more even.

As with any reset, players should check the official patch notes for exact details about what carries over and what does not. Bungie's announcements are the most reliable source for specifics, especially while the update is still being rolled out.

## A Refreshed Economy and New Reward Pass

The in-game economy is also being refreshed as part of the Nightfall update. A healthy economy matters in an extraction shooter because the value of items, the risk of losing equipment and the rewards for successful runs all shape how players make decisions. Adjusting these systems can change how cautious or aggressive players choose to be.

Bungie is also introducing a new NuCal-inspired Reward Pass at no additional cost to players who own the game. This is an important detail, because it means players do not need to spend extra money to access the pass. NuCal-inspired themes give the rewards a distinct visual identity, and the pass offers players another reason to keep playing throughout the season.

Players should still consult the in-game menus and official announcements to see the exact rewards, tiers and duration of the pass, since these details may be updated over time.

## Weapon, Runner and Matchmaking Adjustments

Bungie has outlined adjustments to weapons, Runner abilities and matchmaking activities. Balance changes are a regular part of live-service games, and they help keep matches varied by preventing a small number of options from dominating.

Changes to weapons can affect how players approach combat, which loadouts remain effective and how encounters play out at different distances. Adjustments to Runner abilities can shift the balance between different playstyles, giving players reason to experiment with approaches they may have previously overlooked.

Matchmaking activities are another important part of the update. In an extraction shooter, the quality of matches has a major effect on how enjoyable the game feels, and refinements in this area can lead to fairer and more consistent encounters. Players should read the official notes for exact numbers and changes, as balance details can be revised after release.

## Marathon: Symbiosis Arrives December 8

The next major milestone on the roadmap is Marathon: Symbiosis, planned for December 8, 2026. It represents a significant expansion of what Marathon offers, moving beyond the current experience and introducing content designed to appeal to a broader range of players.

The update is expected to bring the game's first permanent PvE experience, an expanded Perimeter, a new Runner shell named Bishop, a social space and a firing range. Each of these additions serves a different purpose, from new ways to play to practical tools that help players improve and connect with one another.

As with any planned release, dates can change, so players should rely on Bungie's official announcements for the latest confirmation of the schedule and the final list of features.

## The First Permanent PvE Experience

The permanent PvE experience is one of the most important parts of the Symbiosis update. Until now, Marathon has focused on competitive extraction gameplay, where players must balance risk, reward and the threat of other squads. A permanent PvE option gives players a different way to enjoy the game, with the focus placed on cooperative play and challenges rather than direct competition against others.

This addition may appeal to players who enjoy the world and mechanics of Marathon but prefer to avoid constant player-versus-player pressure. It also gives newer players a more approachable place to learn the game's systems before testing themselves in more competitive situations.

The word permanent is significant. It suggests that the PvE experience is intended to be a lasting part of the game rather than a temporary event, and players can expect it to remain available as the game continues to grow.

## Expanded Perimeter, Social Space and Firing Range

The Symbiosis update also includes an expanded Perimeter, a social space and a firing range. These features may seem less dramatic than a new mode, but they can have a real effect on how players experience the game day to day.

An expanded Perimeter gives players more to explore and adds variety to a familiar part of the game. A social space provides a place for players to gather, prepare and interact outside of matches, which helps the game feel more like a community. A firing range offers a useful way to test weapons and practice without the pressure of a live match.

Together, these features support both new and experienced players by making it easier to learn, experiment and connect before heading into the action.

## Meet Bishop, the New Runner Shell

Bishop is a new Runner shell planned for the Symbiosis update, designed around speed and powerful melee attacks. Runner shells define how players approach encounters, and a shell built around mobility and close-range strength gives players another distinct option.

A fast, melee-focused Runner suits players who prefer aggressive, up-close tactics and enjoy using movement to control the flow of a fight. At the same time, players will still need to think about positioning, timing and the threats around them, since speed and melee power do not guarantee success in every situation.

As with other new additions, players should check the official description of Bishop's abilities once the shell is available, since the exact details of its kit may be adjusted before and after release.

## More PvE and PvP Content Planned for March

Bungie has also outlined further connected PvE and PvP experiences for March. This shows that the December update is part of a longer plan rather than a one-time addition, and it gives players an early look at what may come after Symbiosis.

Connecting PvE and PvP experiences suggests that Bungie wants the different parts of the game to feel linked instead of separate. Players who enjoy both styles may find that progress and activities in one area support the other, creating a more unified experience.

Because the March plans are further away, players should treat them as a roadmap rather than a final promise. Details may change, and Bungie's official channels will provide the most accurate updates as the date approaches.

## What Players Should Do to Prepare

Players who want to get the most out of the roadmap can prepare in a few simple ways. The first is to read the official patch notes for the Nightfall Refresh so that they understand exactly how the progression reset, economy changes and balance adjustments affect their play.

It is also worth claiming the new Reward Pass early, since it is available at no extra cost to players who own the game. Spending time with the refreshed progression system can help players build their equipment again and settle on a playstyle that suits them.

Looking ahead to December, players interested in Bishop or the PvE experience may want to follow Bungie's announcements for any further reveals. Staying informed through official channels is more reliable than relying on rumors or unverified claims.

## Why This Roadmap Matters for Marathon

This roadmap shows that Bungie is investing in Marathon for the long term. The Nightfall Refresh improves the existing experience through progression, rewards and balance changes, while Symbiosis adds a new way to play and expands the world with new features.

The free Reward Pass, the refreshed economy and the progression reset make the October update welcoming to both new and returning players. The permanent PvE experience, the expanded Perimeter, Bishop, the social space and the firing range then give players more variety and more reasons to stay.

With further connected PvE and PvP experiences planned for March, the roadmap gives the community a clear sense of direction. Players who want to stay up to date should follow Bungie's official announcements and check the in-game news regularly as each stage of the roadmap arrives.
